title: GTM DACH
description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

Heidi sits in an unusual position. We lead a category being built for the first time. Hundreds of thousands of clinicians found us on their own, started using the product for free and told a colleague. The market is open and the clinicians in it already like the product. Your job is to turn those smaller scale use cases into enterprise deals.

You're the first line to Heidi in DACH. Inbound demand connects you with practices, MVZs and hospital groups already using us, and you decide whether to qualify each one in, out or close it yourself. Where the signals run thin, you build the outbound.

For most clinicians you'll be the first person from Heidi they ever speak to. You'll both triage inbound to your Account Executive where it belongs and close your own deals from day one, because we want people as close to the frontline as possible. You'll build a network across German-speaking healthcare that outlasts the role.

What you’ll do

  • Work the inbound queue and the warm product signals across DACH. Your day goes to clinicians and practices already using Heidi, where the product tells you who's outgrown the free version.

  • Build outbound where the signals are thin: pick the practice groups, MVZs and hospital groups worth going after and work them in German.

  • Research the accounts behind those signals, work out who else in the practice or hospital group needs to be in the conversation, and build the angle for each one.

  • Reach the people the signals point to, across calls, email and social, while the interest is still fresh.

  • Book demos and meetings for your AEs with enough context that nothing is lost in the handoff.

  • Own small SMB deals end to end, from first conversation through to closed.

  • Keep HubSpot accurate, keep the pipeline moving and hit your qualified-lead number every month.

  • Partner with AEs, Marketing, Product, Operations and Customer Success so what you promise on the call matches what clinicians get, and so the German-language product and collateral keep up with what you hear.

  • Track what's shifting in German healthcare (regulation, the practice groups, the insurers, the competitive set) and tell the team what you're hearing on the phones.

What we're looking for

  • Native or fluent German, and English that allows you to work in a global team.

  • You've worked somewhere with a high bar, whether that's tech, sales, creative, banking, consulting, or PE/VC. We care more about what you've achieved than any time in a sales role.

  • You care about what we do. You'd rather learn how the product works than memorise a pitch.

  • You can hold a conversation with anyone and get to the point of it fast. Clinicians have extremely busy schedules, you respect that and still get the meeting.

  • Knowing how German healthcare buys (who decides in a Praxis, an MVZ or a hospital group, and who pays) is a head start. If you don't know it yet, you're the type who'd learn it in your first month.

  • Organised and self-running. You run your own list, your own day and your own follow-ups without being chased.

  • Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping or side projects.

  • You default to building over requesting.

  • You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. Great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them.

 

Attitude is more important than experience so if you are a hungry, competitive and highly motivated operator who has a knack for problem solving and building relationships we want to hear from you.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

title: Compliance Automation Analyst
description:
Superhuman offers a dynamic hybrid working model for this role. This flexible approach gives team members the best of both worlds: plenty of focus time along with in-person collaboration that helps foster trust, innovation, and a strong team culture.

About Superhuman

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites. The company’s products include Grammarly’s writing assistance, Superhuman Docs’s collaborative workspaces, Mail’s inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and delivers help automatically. Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over 40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters. The Opportunity

We’ve consolidated separate compliance programs (Grammarly, Coda, Superhuman Mail, and Superhuman Go) into a single program. We’re rapidly replacing the point-in-time approaches with continuous, automated, code-defined evidence, and this role continues to build on that.

The job is to automate your way out of the manual toil: our GRC automation platform is the evidence-automation backbone, agentic systems (Claude Code and similar) are the force multiplier, and GitHub is where the program lives as code. If your instinct on seeing a manual control-testing process is to turn it into a repeatable, automated pipeline, this role is for you.

What You Will Do:

  • Automate evidence collection. Configure and operate the GRC automation platform: wire up data sources, build evidence plugins, scope data sets, author analysis rules, and stand up continuous monitoring operations, replacing screenshot-and-upload workflows with automated collectors mapped to controls.

  • Automate GRC workflows and run compliance as code. Use Claude Code (or similar) and MCPs for evidence requests, control mapping, gap analysis, vendor reviews, and reporting; build and curate the team’s agent harness; and manage policies, control definitions, and automation in GitHub through branches, pull requests, and review.

  • Design control testing and drive remediation. Instrument testing across SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017/27018, ISO 27701, PCI DSS, and ISO 42001 for continuous assurance rather than point-in-time snapshots, and work with control owners and engineering to close gaps with automated evidence behind every finding.

What Ramping Up Looks Like:

You will be configuring our GRC automation platform, not just clicking through it, within your first few weeks. In your first 90 days, we’d expect you to learn the platform configuration, ship your first automated evidence collectors, retire a batch of manual screenshot evidence, and get at least one agent-assisted workflow running end-to-end.

Why This Role:

  • You’ll design the automation architecture for compliance across four products, rather than maintaining an existing checklist.

  • You get the mandate and the tooling to retire manual evidence collection: a GRC automation platform, agentic AI, and compliance-as-code.

  • We actually run LLMs and AI agents in production GRC workflows today. This is how the team operates day-to-day.

  • Small team, high ownership, and a direct line to Legal and Engineering leadership. You’ll shape the program, not just sustain it.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years in compliance, GRC, or IT audit, hands-on with the frameworks above (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and adjacent).

  • 1+ year using agentic AI systems (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) to do real compliance work, with automation you have delivered, not just prototypes.

  • Comfortable in GitHub: repos, branches, pull requests, and code review. CI/CD familiarity is a strong plus.

  • Fast on new tooling. You can pick up a GRC automation platform and be productive in weeks, configuring it directly rather than relying on others to do so.

  • Deep GRC fluency: control design, evidence, risk, and how auditors actually think.

  • Working knowledge of cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP): IAM, compute, storage, networking, and security controls, because that’s where the evidence lives.

  • Systems thinker who prefers to automate repetitive manual work rather than repeat it.

Nice to Have:

  • Reads APIs, JSON, and logs comfortably; scripting (Python, bash, TypeScript).

  • Prior hands-on experience with a GRC automation platform (Vanta, Drata, or similar).

  • Scripting/light coding and API integration experience.

  • Certifications such as CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, or similar.

  • AI governance, AI risk management, or ISO 42001 exposure.

  • Background in a technology, SaaS, or engineering-adjacent environment.

Support for you, professionally and personally

  • Professional growth: We believe that autonomy and trust are key to empowering our team members to do their best, most innovative work in a way that aligns with their interests, talents, and well-being. We also support professional development and advancement with training, coaching, and regular feedback.

  • A connected team: Superhuman builds a product that helps people connect, and we apply this mindset to our own team. Our remote-first hybrid model enables a highly collaborative culture supported by our values. We work to foster belonging among team members in a variety of ways. This includes our employee resource groups, Superhuman Circles, which promote connection among those with shared identities including BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ team members, women, and parents. We also celebrate our colleagues and accomplishments with global, local, and team-specific programs.

  • Comprehensive benefits for candidates based in Germany: Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing life care (including mental health care and risk benefits) and ample and defined time off. We also offer support to set up a home office, wellness and pet care stipends, learning and development opportunities, and more.

  • Relocation Support: Superhuman provides comprehensive relocation support to make your move to Berlin seamless. Our package includes visa assistance, destination services to help you and your family settle in comfortably, and a relocation bonus to cover additional expenses, such as temporary housing.

     

We encourage you to apply

At Superhuman, we value our differences, and we encourage all to apply. Superhuman is an equal-opportunity company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race or ethnic origin, religion or belief, gender, disability, sexual identity, or age.

We optimise and market a growing portfolio of flexible assets on European power markets - battery storage, aggregated EV fleets and renewable generation. Our multi-market optimisation and execution is purely algorithm-driven and fully automated. What decides whether we make money is the quality of the inputs our algorithms run on: forecasts of prices, market fundamentals and renewable generation - from long-term views down to intraday and real time.

  • You own the complete forecasting stack our short-term algorithmic trading desk relies on: prices (day-ahead, intraday, imbalance and ancillary services such as FCR and aFRR), fundamentals (load, residual load, cross-border flows, outages, fuel and CO₂) and renewable generation (wind and PV) and you keep short-term and long-term views consistent
  • You deliver these forecasts as production-grade, probabilistic inputs (point forecasts, quantiles and scenarios) directly into our optimisation and bidding algorithms, and own their accuracy, timeliness and availability
  • You develop and implement analytical, statistical and fundamental models to assess European power and renewable markets and deliver data-driven insights and signals for our trading decisions
  • You assess market trends and new markets quantitatively, providing the basis for country and product decisions
  • You lead a team of 5-7 analysts & data scientist, develop them technically and coach them in their personal growth
  • You work closely with Trading Desk, Portfolio Management & Pricing, Sales and Product, building the bridge to develop cutting edge products and services
  • You create reports, monitorings and benchmarks to derive actionable insights for trading, senior management and other stakeholders
  • Your models feed into bids and prices largely automatically, and into the decisions of the management board


Who you are

  • Several years of experience in quantitative analysis on European power markets — price, fundamental and renewable generation forecasting as well as fundamental modelling.
  • A solid understanding of day-ahead, intraday and ancillary services, capacity and local flexibility markets, and of how prices form in them
  • Experience in technical leadership — or a clearly visible step towards it — with the ability to motivate and develop a team
  • The ability to translate quantitative findings so that the management board and stakeholders can make decisions based on them
  • business-fluent English and German is a plus

title: Senior CRM Manager:in (Lifecycle & Retention) I E-Commerce I Growth I Achim, hybrid
description:
Kleines Kraftwerk & Du

Wir sind Kleines Kraftwerk, ein junges Unternehmen mit großer Ambition. 


In nur drei Jahren sind wir stark gewachsen und noch lange nicht am Ziel. Bei uns erwarten dich Verantwortung, Tempo und echter Gestaltungsspielraum – verbunden mit der Erwartung, dass du ihn nutzt.  Mit unseren Produkten bringen wir die Energie von morgen direkt zu den Menschen nach Hause. Unsere Mission ist es, nachhaltige Energie einfach, zugänglich und alltagstauglich zu machen. 


Du sorgst dafür, dass die richtige Botschaft zur richtigen Zeit bei den richtigen Kund:innen ankommt und machst sichtbar, welchen Beitrag CRM zu unserem Wachstum leistet.

Als unser:e neue:r


Senior CRM Manager:in /  Lifecycle & Retention

entwickelst du CRM bei uns von einem bislang nebenbei betriebenen Kanal zu einer echten Wachstumsfunktion. Die Basis ist da: Klaviyo, mehrere hunderttausend Leads und Kund:innen sowie jede Menge Daten. Was fehlt, ist eine klare CRM-Strategie mit intelligenter Segmentierung, automatisierten Lifecycle-Flows, strukturiertem Testing und einem Reporting, das Wirkung und Umsatzbeitrag sichtbar macht.

Du verschickst bei uns also nicht einfach Newsletter. Du gestaltest, wie wir entlang des gesamten Lifecycles Kund:innen ansprechen und langfristig binden. Dafür bekommst du echte Ownership, viel Gestaltungsspielraum und die Chance, CRM bei Kleines Kraftwerk von Grund auf zu prägen.

Bereit, aus CRM einen echten Wachstumstreiber zu machen?


Wofür du Verantwortung übernimmst



CRM lief bei uns bisher nebenbei – jetzt wollen wir daraus einen echten Wachstumstreiber machen. 

  • Du baust unsere CRM- und Lifecycle-Strategie auf: Du entwickelst Prozesse, Tools und Strukturen von Grund auf und richtest sie auf Kundenbindung und Wiederkäufe aus.
  • Du entwickelst unsere Lifecycle-Flows: In Klaviyo konzipierst und optimierst du automatisierte Customer Journeys von Welcome und Post-Purchase bis Cross-/Upselling und Win-back.
  • Du entwickelst relevante Kundensegmente: Leads und Kund:innen segmentierst du nach Kaufverhalten, Interessen und Lifecycle-Phase für eine gezielte Kundenansprache.
  • Du verantwortest unsere CRM-Kampagnen: Du steuerst Themen, Timing und Versand und stimmst dich eng mit Marketing und E-Commerce ab.
  • Du etablierst eine Test- und Lernkultur: Mit strukturierten A/B-Tests identifizierst du Optimierungspotenziale und entwickelst unsere CRM-Maßnahmen kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Du steuerst die CRM-Performance: Relevante KPIs und Reportings nutzt du, um Erfolge messbar zu machen und konkrete Maßnahmen abzuleiten.
  • Du stellst Datenqualität und Compliance sicher: Du sorgst für sauberes Listenmanagement und DSGVO-konforme CRM-Prozesse.
  • Du identifizierst die größten CRM-Hebel: Potenziale priorisierst du nach Business Impact und entwickelst perspektivisch weitere Retention-Programme wie Loyalty und Referral.


Womit du punkten kannst

Du kennst CRM nicht nur aus der Theorie. Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung im CRM-, Lifecycle- oder Retention-Marketing mit und weißt, wie aus Kundendaten relevante Kommunikation und messbare Kundenbindung entsteht. Dabei wartest du nicht auf Vorgaben, sondern erkennst Potenziale und setzt sie eigenständig um.

  • Du kennst CRM aus der Praxis: Du bringst ca. 4+ Jahre Erfahrung mit, idealerweise im E-Commerce- oder D2C-Umfeld, und hast eine CRM-Funktion bereits aufgebaut oder maßgeblich weiterentwickelt.
  • Du beherrschst Klaviyo: Flows, Segmentierung, Templates und Testing gehören für dich zum Tagesgeschäft und auch mit großen Kontaktdatenbanken arbeitest du sicher.
  • Du denkst datengetrieben: Du verstehst relevante CRM-KPIs, erkennst Zusammenhänge und leitest daraus konkrete Maßnahmen zur Steigerung von Kundenbindung und Umsatz ab.
  • Du behältst den Überblick und setzt Prioritäten: Kampagnen, Flows, Tests und neue Ideen gleichzeitig bringen dich nicht aus dem Takt. Du entscheidest eigenständig, wo der größte Hebel liegt.
  • Du willst gestalten statt verwalten: Du hast den Anspruch, CRM aktiv aufzubauen, Strukturen zu schaffen und bestehende Ansätze kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.
  • Du kommunizierst souverän: Du arbeitest eng mit unterschiedlichen Teams zusammen und kannst dich auf Deutsch sehr sicher und klar verständigen.

Bewirb dich nicht, wenn …

  • du ein fertiges CRM-Setup mit bestehenden Prozessen und Playbooks übernehmen möchtest – bei uns baust du vieles selbst auf.
  • du lange Freigabeprozesse einer schnellen, direkten Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsführung vorziehst.
  • du ausschließlich Kampagnen versenden möchtest, ohne Verantwortung für Segmentierung, Testing und Reporting zu übernehmen.
  • Datenarbeit für dich eher Pflicht als Werkzeug ist und du ausschließlich kreativ arbeiten möchtest.
  • fehlende Prozesse und Unklarheit dich eher stressen als motivieren – ein fertiges CRM-Handbuch gibt es bei uns noch nicht.


Worauf du dich freuen kannst

  • CRM aufbauen statt nur verwalten: Du bekommst volle Gestaltungsfreiheit beim Aufbau unserer CRM-Funktion und kannst Strukturen, Prozesse und Maßnahmen von Grund auf mitgestalten.
  • Eine Datenbasis mit echtem Potenzial: Dich erwartet eine große und stetig wachsende Kontaktbasis – eine seltene Ausgangslage, um mit CRM schnell sichtbare und messbare Ergebnisse zu erzielen.
  • Gemeinsam möchten wir wachsen: Wir setzen auf ein starkes WIR-Gefühl, eine freundschaftliche Teamkultur, flache Hierarchien und kurze Entscheidungswege.
  • Raum für deine Ideen: Deine Ideen werden gehört und gebraucht – du kannst dich einbringen, Verantwortung übernehmen und wirklich mitgestalten.
  • Work-Life-Balance ist uns wichtig: du hast flexible Arbeitszeiten, 2 Tage Home-Office pro Woche, 28 Tage Urlaub sowie 5 Tage Workation im Jahr, außerdem hast du an deinem Geburtstag frei!
  • Deine Gesundheit und Zukunft liegen uns am Herzen: Du erhältst Zuschüsse zu Wellpass und betrieblicher Altersvorsorge sowie exklusive Rabatte auf unsere Produkte.
  • Ein Arbeitsplatz zum Wohlfühlen: Dich erwarten moderne, lichtdurchflutete Büros und eine phänomenale Dachterrasse, die zum Durchatmen und Austauschen einlädt.


Du willst Teil der Energiewende werden?

Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der erneuerbaren Energien.  Join uns und werde Teil des Teams!

Wir sind ein ambitioniertes Start-up im Bereich erneuerbare Energien mit einer klaren Mission: erneuerbare Energie von morgen für alle zugänglich machen. Dafür suchen wir Menschen, die Verantwortung übernehmen, eigene Ideen einbringen und Lust haben, gemeinsam mit uns zu wachsen: in einer dynamischen Umgebung, in der du viel Gestaltungsspielraum hast, Strukturen mit aufbauen kannst, eigene Entscheidungen triffst und direkten Einfluss auf den Erfolg des Unternehmens nimmst. 

Dabei ist uns egal, woher du kommst, an was du glaubst, wen du liebst, womit du dich identifizierst, wie alt du bist, ob du neurodivers bist oder eine Behinderung hast – die Welt ist bunt und wir können es kaum erwarten, von dir zu lesen! Alle Geschlechter sind Willkommen!

Who we are


NeuroNation is the personalised training app that empowers more than 20 million people all over the world in staying brain healthy and happy in their lives.

We collaborate closely with scientists and universities to achieve the best results possible. Our engaging apps have received awards from major health insurance companies, such as the AOK, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Health. Also, we've been awarded by Apple and Google as one of the best apps available.


To improve the training experience our app provides and make the product more effective and engaging to users and patients, we are looking for a passionate person with a background in science and deep interest in digital health and games. Since the role touches many different fields, you don’t have to bring all know-how already with you - we are welcoming passionate learners who want to develop themselves in this role.


So, if you want to help us shape a better tomorrow, join us on our journey!


Your roles and responsibilities


  • Improve the training experience and the exercises of our mobile and web app by making NeuroNation as effective and engaging as possible
  • Continuously incorporate the latest findings from neuroscience by reading scientific papers and learning from concepts that have been proven to have impact on clinical outcomes
  • Apply User Research and Usability Testing to learn how we can best help users and patients, and define useful features and visual concepts
  • Collaborate with our scientific partners from various universities and clinics to run successful clinical trials with NeuroNation

title: Product Manager*in (m/w/d)
description:
Lust auf Produktgestaltung und Innovation?

Willst du Features bauen oder echte Probleme lösen?
Wir suchen keinen bloßen „Verwalter von Anforderungen“, sondern einen strategischen Kopf, der unser Produkt zum Marktführer macht. Wir sind ein SaaS-Startup mit einer klaren Mission: Mehrweg in der Logistik so einfach wie Einweg zu machen. Wir reduzieren nicht nur den CO₂-Fußabdruck einer ganzen Branche, sondern optimieren einen ihrer nervigsten Prozesse.

Als Product Manager bist du nicht dafür da, Tickets zu schreiben. Du bist dafür verantwortlich, dass unser Produkt wertvoll für den Kunden und rentabel für unser Business ist.

Aufgaben

  • Product Discovery statt bloßer Ausführung: Du bekommst keine fertigen Lösungen vorgesetzt. Stattdessen arbeitest du eng mit Design und Engineering zusammen, um herauszufinden, was wir bauen müssen. Du validierst Hypothesen schnell und minimierst das Risiko, Dinge zu bauen, die niemand braucht.
  • Outcome über Output: Dein Erfolg misst sich nicht an der Anzahl der geschriebenen Tickets oder pünktlichen Releases, sondern an messbaren Geschäftsergebnissen (z.B. Adoption-Rate von Features, Prozess-Effizienz beim Kunden).
  • Tiefes Kundenverständnis: Du wirst zum Experten für unsere Nutzer. Durch kontinuierliche User Interviews und Datenanalysen verstehst du deren Schmerzpunkte besser als sie selbst und leitest daraus die Produktstrategie ab.
  • Business Viability: Du stellst sicher, dass unsere Lösungen nicht nur nutzbar sind, sondern auch in unser Geschäftsmodell passen und rechtlich sowie technisch realisierbar sind.

Qualifikation

  • Liebe zum Problem: Du verstehst den Unterschied zwischen Projekt- und Produktmanagement. Du liebst es, komplexe Probleme zu lösen und übernimmst Verantwortung für den wirtschaftlichen Erfolg deines Produktbereichs.
  • Evidenzbasierte Entscheidungen: Du verlässt dich nicht auf Bauchgefühl. Du hast Erfahrung mit modernen Discovery-Methoden (Prototyping, A/B-Testing, Customer Interviews) und weißt, wie man Daten nutzt, um Argumente zu stützen.
  • Kollaboration & Kommunikation: Du siehst Entwickler und Designer nicht als "Ressourcen", sondern als Partner. Du kannst Stakeholdern souverän "Nein" sagen, um den Fokus auf das Wesentliche zu wahren, und kannst deine Produktvision begeisternd vermitteln.
  • Hintergrund: Ein Studium ist gut, echte Erfahrung ist besser. Ob Informatik, BWL oder Quereinsteiger: Wichtig ist, dass du Erfahrung im Bauen digitaler Produkte (SaaS) hast und idealerweise schon einmal in einem schnelllebigen Umfeld (Startup) gearbeitet hast.

Benefits

  • Dein Buden-Buddy, unsere Welcome-Box sowie eine strukturierte Einführungsphase helfen dir dich schnell bei uns zurechtzufinden und bei uns anzukommen.
  • Du erlebst eine positive Teamkultur durch regelmäßige Buden-Spieleabende, wöchentliche Coffee Dates, gemeinsame sportliche Aktivitäten (Firmenläufe,…), spannende Sommerevents, u.v.m.
  • Bei der Wahl deines Arbeitsstandorts sind wir flexibel und du entscheidest, ob du ins Büro kommen möchtest oder von Zuhause aus arbeiten möchtest.
  • Wir wollen gemeinsam „groß“ werden und freuen uns, wenn du Teil der Reise bist und aktiv an der Entwicklung der Bude mitwirkst.
  • Deine Arbeit hat einen nachhaltigen Impact, denn wir verkleinern den CO2-Fußabdruck der Logistik.
  • Wähle die Incentives, die zu dir passen: Wir bezuschussen das Deutschland-Ticket, EGYM Wellpass und das Jobrad.

title: Senior Sales Director
description:
Life at Plume

At Plume, we believe that technology isn't about moving faster, it's about making life's moments better. Which is why we've built the world's first, and only, open and hardware-independent service delivery platform for smart homes, small businesses, enterprises, and beyond. Our SaaS platform uses WiFi, advanced AI, and machine learning to create the future of connected spaces—and human experiences—at massive scale.

We now deliver services to over 60 million locations globally and have managed over 3 billion devices on our platform. We're expanding rapidly, pioneering a new category, and we achieved our Series F funding in just four years. Our customers include many of the world's largest Internet Service Providers (ISPs) who look to Plume to help them evolve their smart home offerings while gleaning insights from their own data. 

With a bias for action and a love for being trailblazers, the team at Plume embodies a combination of relentless curiosity and imaginative innovation. We challenge ourselves to think in ways that other companies don't, work to do what should be done (rather than what can), and if we can't do it exceptionally well, we don't do it. It's how we've assembled a team of world-class builders, thinkers, and doers. And it's how we're reinventing what's possible every day.

Role Description:
Plume works with Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to run the connected experience inside their
subscribers' homes and small businesses. Our platform sits between their network and the people using
it, managing WiFi performance, security, device visibility, care and the digital services layered on top. We
are used at scale by some of the largest ISPs across North America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
The UK and Ireland are mature and concentrated markets. The number of ISPs that matter is small, they
are well known to us, and most already have an established approach to managing the connected home.
Success here depends on building credibility at a senior level, shaping how these organisations think
about the experience they deliver to their subscribers, and then proving that value at scale.
We are looking for someone who is at their best in a small number of large, complex accounts rather
than in a broad prospecting territory.
It is a role with real ownership. You will be the face of Plume in the region, working directly with our
executive team and with senior leaders at some of the best-known ISPs in the market.

Responsibilities:
• A named list of UK and Ireland ISPs, covering both new logos and the growth of existing
deployments into new services, subscriber tiers and lines of business.
• A multi-million-dollar annual quota carried across new business and installed base expansion.
• The full cycle: executive access, discovery, business case, technical validation and POC,
commercial modelling, procurement, contract, and a clean handover into delivery. You stay
accountable through launch.
• The relationship map inside each account. Not a single champion, but the CTO, the Chief Product
or Consumer officer, the owner of customer care and operations, and whoever holds the broadband
P&L.
• A virtual team pulled from solutions engineering, product, delivery, finance, legal and executive
sponsorship. You direct it. You do not wait for it.
• Accurate forecasting. Deals of this size move, and we would rather know early than late.
• A clear read on the market: how ISPs in the region are approaching the connected home, where
their priorities are shifting, and what that means for our roadmap. You are our eyes in the territory.

Qualifications:
This role calls for someone who already understands how ISPs buy. Their decision cycles, stakeholder
structures and commercial models are specific to the industry, and the experience we are looking for
reflects that.
• A track record selling hardware, software, cloud or platform solutions directly to ISPs, with evidence
of recurring or subscription-based commercial models. Your experience should be with ISPs as the
buyer, rather than with a telco's enterprise IT function as one account among many.
• Ownership of deals in the multi-million-dollar ACV range, with 9 to 24 month cycles, formal
procurement, and an established solution already in place.
• Fluency in ISP economics. ARPU and attach rates, churn and retention drivers, cost to serve,
contact volumes and handling time, truck roll avoidance, CPE fleet lifecycle and ODM relationships,
NPS. You should be able to build a credible business case yourself before a solutions engineer is in
the room.
• Experience winning business where the customer already had a solution in place, whether bought
or built in-house. That is a different commercial conversation, and we place real weight on it.

Create compelling campaigns, brands and experiences for causes that matter. You'll be a senior member of the London team bringing in new clients and, as a leader, defining and improving the work we're creating. You will also be a part of our global creative director team who meet regularly for creative inspiration.

  1. 6+ years in senior creative role, ideally with hands-on designing experience. At least some of this experience working on fundraising and mobilisation campaigns.

Skills and experience

  • Proven experience as a senior copywriter, content strategist, or content lead in an agency, in-house team, or content studio.

  • Excellent writing and editing skills across long and short form — from thought leadership articles to headlines, emails, and social posts.

  • Confidence working with senior stakeholders and turning competing requests into clear, prioritised content plans.
  • Strong organisation and the ability to manage multiple requests at pace, including triaging briefs and managing stakeholder expectations.
  • Genuine interest in what AI can do for content and creativity, with awareness of the ethical and legal considerations involved.

Useful but not essential

  • Experience with Pencil or an equivalent AI creative platform (training on Pencil will be provided).
  • Background in financial services, payments, fintech, or B2B technology.

  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows for yourself and others to improve efficiency and output quality.
  • Ability to train others on effective AI tool use and share best practice across the team.
  • Agentic approach to complex, multi-step content challenges — breaking briefs into components and finding efficient, high-quality routes to delivery.

Our Global Structure

Money is DoorDash's organisation responsible for the financial products and infrastructure that enable transactions across DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo. The domain owns how consumers pay, how merchants and couriers are paid, and how money is recorded, reconciled and reported, covering payment processing, payment methods, payouts, invoicing, financial ledgers and regulatory compliance.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help scale Money Domain. You will lead important engineering wide initiatives across Invoicing Platform, Payment Instruments, amongst others; working with Engineering, Product, Operations, and business leaders to deliver dependable, scalable Money capabilities for the business. Programs will span backend services, partner and merchant integrations, and regulatory / compliance products. They require strong technical judgment, cross organisational coordination, stakeholder management, and ownership of results.

You will report into the centralised global Technical Program Management team in Engineering, through a manager based in London. This is a hybrid role based in our London office in Cannon Street.

  • Drive Money Domain's Most Strategic Programs - You will partner closely with Engineering and Product leadership, Strategy & Operations, and cross-functional teams to turn Money Domain's strategy into executable technical programs.

We're excited about you because…

  • You're experienced in working with engineering teams on  large-scale distributed systems and/or b2b products. You can speak to system architecture, scalability and reliability decisions, and design trade offs.
  • You're a strong leader with the ability to collaborate and build relationships across organizations, bridge gaps between teams, and successfully influence without authority.
  • You have strong ownership, urgency, and drive. You are willing to roll up your sleeves and dive into the details to understand and drive your programs.

description:

Street Group is a fast-moving B2B SaaS business, grown in Manchester but on a UK-wide mission to make moving house as easy as buying a car. We're PE-backed and scaling fast with an ambitious growth plan, and we're looking for an FP&A Analyst to help us get there.


As we grow, our revenue streams are becoming more varied by the month. That means more reporting, more complexity, and a finance function that needs to proactively help drive growth.


This is an opportunity to help expand our FP&A function, you won't be slotting into a fixed process. You'll be shaping it while owning the data and supporting the models that feed our board packs and investor reporting.


If you want ownership early, enjoy explaining what the numbers mean as much as producing them, and already use AI to take the manual work out of finance, we think you might do great work here.


Why this role exists now


We're growing quickly, and our finance team is growing with us. As our revenue streams expand, so does the appetite for clear, timely insight from our board and investors. That's where you come in. Join us early, help shape how FP&A works here, and see your work make a real difference from day one.


The role

You'll work closely with our FP&A Lead and the wider finance team, owning the data behind our FP&A outputs and turning it into insight the business can act on.

Day-to-day, that means owning our performance trackers and reporting models, drafting the monthly board and management packs, and supporting VCP performance and reporting. You'll help implement new tools and own the data behind them, build dashboards to track commercial and financial performance, and reconcile data across multiple systems so everything stays accurate and consistent.

You'll also support three-statement modelling and our annual budget and rolling forecast cycles, and pick up ad hoc commercial insight and improvement projects as they come up. Throughout, you'll use Claude to automate routine reporting and modelling, so your time goes on the insight that matters.


Who we're looking for

  • 2-4 years in an FP&A, commercial finance or analytical role, and part-qualified or newly qualified (ACA, ACCA or CIMA).

  • A meticulous and detail-driven individual with a strict commitment to accuracy and precision in all financial modelling and reporting.

  • Experience building driver-based models for budgets and forecasts, and producing management information or board and management packs.

  • A solid understanding of double-entry and comfort with three-statement modelling.

  • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, including complex formulas and sensitivity and scenario modelling.

  • An AI-native mindset: you already use Claude, Copilot or a similar tool in your finance work, and you would rather simplify and automate a manual process than plough through it.

  • The ability to explain numbers in plain language to non-finance stakeholders.

  • Someone self-motivated and comfortable managing their own workload without close oversight.

  • SaaS, subscription or tech experience is a bonus, not a requirement. Time at a growing, PE-backed business would be particularly interesting to us.

Why you might not want to apply

  • We'd rather be honest up front, because this role won't be for everyone.

  • If you want clearly defined, settled role boundaries , ours are still forming and will keep evolving as we scale.

  • If you'd rather process numbers than own and explain them. This role is about the story behind the figures as much as the figures themselves.

  • If pace, ambiguity and shifting priorities aren't for you. We move quickly, and priorities change as the business grows.

Who are Street Group?

We're an award-winning PropTech business based in Manchester, founded in 2015 by brother and sister duo, Tom & Heather Staff. Most of us have personal experience of how painful moving can be, and Tom and Heather saw an opportunity to change this: utilising technology, as well as our incredibly talented team, to improve the industry for everyone.

Our products, Street.co.uk, Spectre & Cortex, form a powerful trio, working harmoniously together to transform an agent's job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging 1,000s of agencies across the UK.

We recognise that women and people from underrepresented groups often apply for jobs only when they meet every single requirement listed. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application!

Why join Street Group?

description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Department Description

Allica's Product teams own the end-to-end product experience across Payments, Financial Crime, Lending, Deposits, Digital Tools and much more - working daily with a wide range of third-party suppliers whose services are woven into the heart of what we build. Managing those relationships well is a competitive advantage, and it's governed by Allica's Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) framework, with active review cycles running quarterly to annually.

You'll be the person who keeps Product's supplier relationships running like clockwork - spotting what needs attention before it becomes a problem and giving the team the confidence that nothing's falling through the cracks. Working closely with TPRM, Compliance, Legal and Procurement teams, you'll build a reputation as the go-to person who makes things happen across the business.

Role Description

As Supplier Coordinator/Analyst, you'll be at the centre of how Product manages its suppliers - making sure Allica stays on top of every review, renewal and requirement across a fast-growing supplier estate, in line with our TPRM framework.

This is an individual contributor role built for someone who thrives on staying ahead of things: you're the person Product comes to for a clear answer on what's due and what's outstanding, and the one who catches a licence, renewal or review before it becomes due.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Own the administrative lifecycle of periodic supplier reviews (quarterly, bi-annual, annual depending upon tier) - chasing and collating required inputs from suppliers and internal stakeholders

  • Draft review paperwork and flag obvious risks or gaps for the Product Owner to assess and sign off

  • Track outstanding actions arising from reviews through to closure, so nothing falls through the cracks between cycles

  • Track licence and contract renewal dates across the Product supplier estate and raise renewals in good time

  • Complete renewal paperwork and liaise with Legal and Procurement teams

  • Raise ad hoc requests such as additional licences or user seats for platforms as needed by the team

  • Keep supplier records accurate and up to date in internal systems, acting as the source-of-truth checkpoint for audit and review purposes

  • Identify repetitive data-collection tasks across the review cycle and build automation or templates to reduce manual effort

  • Act as the go-to point of contact for Product individuals on all things supplier management, coordinating directly with internal teams

  • Support new vendor onboarding administration - coordinating legal and compliance approvals and owning the onboarding process end to end, while the Product Owner/tribe lead retains ownership of budget and contract terms

  • Document and monitor the data sources shared with vendors, maintaining an accurate, easily queryable record (e.g. via Gatekeeper) in place of ad hoc spreadsheet exercises, working closely with Product Owners who hold the detailed knowledge of what is shared

  • Support the tracking and management of Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) linked to supplier data sharing, ensuring assessments are current and reviewed on schedule

  • Apply controls around requests to extend or add new data sources shared with suppliers, ensuring appropriate sign-off is obtained before any extension

Personal Attributes & Experience

  • Some exposure to supplier, vendor or contract administration, ideally within a regulated or financial services environment

  • Highly organised with strong attention to detail; comfortable chasing multiple stakeholders and suppliers without letting things slip

  • Confident with Excel and internal systems (e.g. Confluence, JIRA); quick to pick up new tools

description:
About Freetrade

Freetrade’s mission is to become the default place to invest. Investing has been too complicated and expensive for too long, keeping millions from making the most of their savings.

We’re changing that.

We’re building our team and looking for people who are excited to reshape how our customers invest and grow their wealth. If you’re driven by solving complex problems and building innovative products, you’ll fit right in.

2026 is a big year for us. Last year, we announced a game changing deal to become part of the IG Group. We’ll continue to operate as an independent business while gaining access to the resources and support of an established leader in the space.

This year, we’re accelerating our roadmap and taking our products to the next level. We’re building new features like mutual funds, bonds, and family investment tools. We’re also exploring how we can leverage AI to deliver an even better experience for our customers.

About the Role

As a Customer Operations Associate, you’ll join our Transfers team within Operations, where your initial focus will be on building deep expertise in transfers and delivering great outcomes for our customers.

You’ll help customers move their investment accounts and assets into and out of Freetrade, owning cases from start to finish and working with customers, external counterparties and teams across the business to make sure transfers are completed accurately, efficiently and within the required timelines.

This is detailed, deadline-driven work where accuracy, ownership and follow-through really matter. You’ll develop a strong understanding of the rules and regulations governing ISA transfers, alongside the operational processes involved in cash and stock transfers, valuations, asset acceptance and CREST. You will also build experience across areas such as JISAs, fund transfers and European stock transfers.

At the centre of the role is genuine care about getting the customer the right outcome. We’re looking for people who take ownership, care deeply about the experience customers have and are willing to follow a problem through until it’s resolved.

Your initial focus will be Transfers, but our longer-term ambition is to build a more cross-trained and flexible Operations team. As you develop, there may be opportunities to gain exposure to other areas such as Payments, Corporate Actions, Trading & Settlements, Customer Service and Complaints, helping you build a broader understanding of how Operations works and how different workflows connect.

This isn’t a rotation programme, and there’s no set timeline or expectation that you’ll move between teams. Opportunities to broaden your knowledge will depend on your development, team priorities and the needs of the business.

Our aim is to develop operators with both depth and breadth across Operations - people who understand their own area deeply, can connect the dots across different workflows and use that knowledge to get better outcomes for customers.

AI and automation are a real part of how Operations is evolving at Freetrade. We’re looking for people who are genuinely enthusiastic about using technology to continuously improve their work - actively finding ways to work faster and smarter and contributing to automation and efficiency improvements as they go.

What You'll Do

  • Own transfer cases from start to finish, helping customers move ISA, JISA, GIA and SIPP accounts and assets into and out of Freetrade, with a focus on accuracy and a smooth customer outcome

  • Process transfer applications accurately and within agreed SLAs.

  • Process valuations and provide acceptance of assets within agreed SLAs.

  • Chase and monitor transfer progress with external counterparties and customers, taking ownership of cases through to completion.

  • Build a strong working knowledge of ISA and SIPP transfer rules, regulations and operational requirements.

  • Work with CREST processes and develop your understanding of stock and asset transfers.

  • Provide technical support to our Customer Service team, helping them answer customer queries accurately and efficiently.

  • Communicate clearly with customers through email and in-app chat and, as our support channels evolve, potentially phone.

  • Keep clear, accurate records of the cases you handle to support quality, compliance and audit standards.

  • Spot patterns in the cases and queries you handle, identifying process gaps and opportunities to improve the customer experience.

  • Review procedures and contribute to process enhancements, challenging inefficient ways of working and helping make things better.

  • Use AI tools as a core part of your day-to-day workflow, actively looking for practical ways to improve your productivity, quality and the efficiency of the wider team.

  • Support the wider Transfers team with ad-hoc tasks and changing priorities when needed.

  • Work closely with your workflow lead to align on priorities and flag anything getting in the way of good customer outcomes.

  • Support newer joiners as your own knowledge and experience grow.

  • Champion a customer-first mindset in everything you do, treating every case with the same level of care you would expect if it were your own account.

About you

  • A genuinely customer-obsessed mindset, with a strong desire to deliver the right outcome and a great experience for every customer

  • Exceptional attention to detail, recognising that the processes you’ll work on are critical to the business and can have regulatory and customer implications if not completed accurately

  • The ability to work independently and proactively, taking ownership of your workload and following cases through to completion

  • Strong judgement and ownership, with the confidence to make good decisions while knowing when something needs to be escalated

  • Experience with, or knowledge of, CREST transfers would be beneficial, alongside knowledge of ISA transfers, JISAs, fund transfers or European stock transfers

description:

You’ll work alongside leaders like Ben, Abs, Sabrina, and Rebe.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.


Why We Need a Platform Security Engineer Now

Omnea takes security seriously. In an era where exploits and supply chain attacks are being discovered and conducted faster than ever before, it’s vital that we stay on the cutting edge of keeping our systems and our customers’ data safe.

 

Hardening our systems is only part of the solution. As we scale out to more industries with their diverse security requirements, we want another individual who can help us attain and maintain higher levels of compliance certification.

 

What We're Looking For

We're hiring at both Level 3 (Senior) and Level 4 (Staff). For calibration, candidates typically bring 5+ years of platform engineering experience in high-growth, cloud-native SaaS environments, but we care more about impact than years. We’re looking for that “T”-shaped skillset where the candidate’s depth is in Cloud Security.

 

Furthermore, the ideal candidate will have a product engineering background but caught the bug for security and cares deeply about enabling people to work fast, safely. Finally, we’re looking for someone who sees security as an enabler and force-multiplier and answers questions with a “Yes, here’s how we do it securely” attitude as opposed to the flat “No” security teams are too often renowned for.

 

What You'll Do

  • Implement and take ownership of our Security roadmap. Working with the Platform Lead, a successful candidate will steadily take ownership over the Platform Security Roadmap, leading implementations and experiments to level up Omnea’s security posture.

  • Own Security Tooling. From safe-chain plugins to SAST/DAST tooling, we want someone who’s keen to get stuck in, onboard, and evolve our tooling to ensure our posture stays at the bleeding edge.

  • Deliver Compliance Programs. Omnea plans to tackle multiple additional compliance certifications to enable the business to serve some of the most regulated industries on the planet. You’ll have a massive hand in making sure we’re up to those standards.

  • Collaborate with our DevX streams. Omnea ships fast, and we want to ship even faster. Making sure we can enable that safely and securely will become your wheelhouse.

  • Implement hardening patterns. See an area where code security could be improved? Let’s do it, and do it in a way that can be scaled out across the entire codebase and easily implemented by the rest of the engineering staff.


What Can You Expect?

  • A strong team. You'll join a platform team of senior and staff engineers who set a high bar and will push you to do your best work.

  • Modern, cloud-native stack. Everything serverless and IaC-driven (AWS, Pulumi, TypeScript end-to-end).

  • Continuous delivery. We deploy multiple times a day. Your work determines how fast and safely the whole engineering org ships.

  • Scalability challenges. As we 10x revenue, you'll be a part of evolving our infrastructure to defend against new security threats and keep us one step ahead.

  • Customer impact. Delivering on our compliance goals and successfully handling audits.

  • Massive ownership. You own problems end-to-end, from brainstorming through to production.

  • Collaboration & autonomy. Plenty of heads-down technical work, but also close partnership with product engineers and engineering leadership.


About You

  • Platform engineer & builder. You design reliable infrastructure and write clean production code (TypeScript or similar). You've built and maintained CI/CD pipelines, IaC, and security gates at scale.

  • Cloud-native. Deep knowledge of AWS (Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge, IAM, networking), or equivalent cloud-native experience. You understand serverless and its trade-offs.

  • Security as an enabler. You think about engineers and business as your customers. You automate toil, improve feedback loops, and care deeply about making other people productive.

  • Commercially minded. You understand that infrastructure & security exist to serve the product and the business. You make trade-offs with that in mind.

  • Bias for action. You iterate quickly, ship pragmatically, and automate everything.

  • Culture carrier. You coach teammates, share knowledge freely, and keep calm when things break.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with Pulumi or similar IaC frameworks.

  • ISC2 (any level) certification.

  • Experience running SaaS compliance programs (ISO:27001, SOC 2 Type II).

  • Open-source contributions to security, infrastructure, or developer tooling projects.

description:
Ready to build data platforms, not just pipelines?

 

At Opencast, we believe great data engineering is about more than moving and transforming data. It's about creating reliable, scalable foundations that help organisations make better decisions and deliver better services. 

 

Our consultants tackle complex engineering challenges across integration, migration, modelling and platform design, working with Microsoft Fabric, Azure and modern data technologies. We value engineering craft, thoughtful problem-solving and building solutions that are simple, robust and built to last. 

 

As our data engineering capability continues to grow, you'll have the opportunity to influence its direction through delivery, mentoring, recruitment and technical leadership. If you're looking for a role where you can shape both solutions and the capability around them, we'd love to hear from you. 

 

The role

  

Opencast data engineers help organisations transform how they manage, use and learn from data. The work ranges from building modern lakehouse and warehouse platforms in Microsoft Fabric to modernising legacy environments, migrating complex workloads and improving the quality, governance and reliability of critical data services.  

 

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full data lifecycle, combining platform design, engineering, integration and optimisation. Expect to work with structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, building batch and near real-time data pipelines that underpin critical business and public services.  

 

You'll collaborate with architects, analysts, software engineers and client teams to solve complex challenges and influence technical direction. The role also offers opportunities to contribute beyond delivery through mentoring, recruitment, community building and helping to define engineering standards and best practice as our capability continues to grow. 

 
 

Requirements

 
This role involves weekly on-site work, and you’ll be required to travel regularly to client locations across the UK. We’re looking for people who value in-person collaboration, enjoy building strong relationships, and are passionate about delivering solutions that make a real difference for our clients.
 
Due to the nature of this role, you must either hold active Security Check (SC) clearance or be eligible and willing to undergo the clearance process. 
 
SC clearance is granted in line with UK Government security vetting requirements. Typically, applicants must have UK citizenship and have lived continuously in the UK for at least the past five years, with no single absence exceeding 28 consecutive days. Nationality and immigration status may also be considered as part of the vetting process. We are unable to progress applications from candidates who do not meet these requirements.
 
If you are unsure whether you meet the eligibility criteria, we encourage you to review the guidance or discuss this with us before applying.
 

We are recruiting for multiple positions, with opportunities available immediately and in the coming months. If you are interested in joining Opencast, we encourage you to apply. 

 
 

Essential experience

 
 
We're looking for engineers who enjoy solving complex technical problems and care about building solutions that are robust, scalable and built to last. 
 
Experience in the following areas is important: 
  • Microsoft Fabric and Azure data services, including lakehouse, warehouse, notebooks and pipeline capabilities.  
  • Building enterprise-scale data platforms, lakehouses and data warehouses.  
  • Data modelling and dimensional modelling techniques such as Kimball. 
  • ETL/ELT development and large-scale data integration.  
  • PySpark, Spark SQL and modern transformation techniques.  
  • Advanced SQL and relational databases including SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Oracle. 
  • Integrating structured, semi-structured and unstructured data sources.  
  • Migration and modernisation of legacy platforms such as Oracle, SQL Server/SSIS or Synapse.  
  • Power BI semantic models, curated datasets and supporting analytics platforms. 
  • Data quality, governance, metadata management and lineage. 
  • Data security, classification and access control approaches. 
  • Automated testing, validation, reconciliation testing and performance optimisation. 
  • DataOps, CI/CD and version control practices.  
  • Agile delivery environments. 
 

Essential consulting skills

 
 

Our clients look to us for more than technical delivery. 

 

Success in this role comes from being able to navigate ambiguity, solve difficult problems and help clients make confident technical decisions. The strongest consultants combine technical expertise with curiosity, pragmatism and a collaborative mindset. 

 

You'll thrive in this role if you enjoy: 

  • Solving complex engineering challenges and exploring different approaches to finding the right solution.  

  • Influencing technical direction through expertise, evidence and constructive challenge.  

  • Working closely with technical and non-technical stakeholders to understand underlying problems rather than simply implement requirements.  

  • Balancing engineering quality, governance, security and reliability with business outcomes.  

  • Sharing knowledge, mentoring others and helping raise engineering standards.  

  • Building trusted relationships with clients and acting as a technical advisor.  

  • Keeping pace with emerging technologies and evaluating new approaches where they can add value.  

  • Contributing to a growing engineering capability while remaining close to delivery and technology. 

 

 

Salary

 
£61,000 - £70,000 per annum.
 

What we offer


A competitive package including a 7% employer pension contribution, share options, and a discretionary bonus. You’ll also benefit from 25 days’ holiday and access to 3 annual “life happens” days to support unexpected situations.  We provide wellbeing support, ongoing professional development, volunteering opportunities, and the chance to be part of a genuinely supportive team.

Where you’ll work


This role requires regular on-site attendance at our HQ, hub offices, and client sites, as well as the ability to work from home. Applicants must be able to travel to offices and client sites across the UK as part of their normal working arrangements, as travel is essential for fulfilling the responsibilities of the role.

We include you


We welcome candidates from all identities, attributes, ways of thinking and backgrounds to thrive in a career at Opencast. Our aim is for the diversity of our people to be reflected in the solutions we deliver, to help create a fairer society for all.   

Interview


Interviews will be conducted via Microsoft Teams. We’re happy to make adjustments to support your needs.
 

Want to know more?  


Visit our website or email

  • High UI/UX craft and strong product taste. You can evaluate whether an interface is not only visually polished, but also usable, accessible, flexible, and maintainable.

  • Experience building or maintaining component libraries, Storybook documentation, visual regression workflows, design-token pipelines, Figma workflows/plugins, or similar design-engineering infrastructure.

  • Strong accessibility fundamentals, including semantic HTML, ARIA patterns, keyboard interaction models, focus management, and inclusive component states.

  • Strong communication skills. You can explain technical and design-system decisions clearly to both specialists and non-specialists.

  • A portfolio or body of work showing shipped design-engineering impact: production UI, component systems, prototypes, Storybook examples, design-system documentation, or code-backed product work.

Bonus points

  • Experience consolidating fragmented component libraries or aligning Figma libraries with production code.

  • Experience using AI-assisted coding or design tools to accelerate prototyping, refactoring, and product iteration.

What you’ll bring to Front

  • A builder’s bias: you prefer to make ideas real in code, learn from how they behave, and iterate quickly.

title: Senior Product Manager - F/H
description:
Le Product Management, c'est notre ADN.

Chez Hubvisory, tu ne te contentes pas de gérer un backlog : tu deviens la référence produit incontournable pour accompagner nos clients grands comptes dans la transformation de leurs produits digitaux et de leurs organisations. Ton rôle est d'allier vision stratégique et excellence opérationnelle pour délivrer de la valeur tangible dans des environnements complexes.

Ce que tu fais concrètement :

  • Tu prends la main sur un périmètre produit à fort enjeu business. Tu analyses les processus en place, tu identifies les leviers d'amélioration réels et tu formalises une vision produit et une feuille de route alignées sur les priorités métier.

  • Tu décides avec la donnée. Tu mesures l'effet de tes arbitrages sur l'usage et la performance commerciale, tu construis les indicateurs qui manquent, et tu transformes une analyse en recommandation argumentée. Pas en tableau de bord de plus.

  • Tu traduis le besoin métier en produit. Exigences fonctionnelles, user stories, critères d'acceptation, priorisation que tu assumes et que tu sais défendre.

  • Tu interviens sur le socle SI. Tu contribues au cadrage et à l'évolution des briques applicatives concernées, en gardant la main sur le pourquoi quand tout le monde discute du comment.

  • Tu alignes un écosystème dense. Métiers, produit, data, IT : tu fais converger des parties prenantes multiples vers des décisions cohérentes, et tu accompagnes l'adoption des solutions auprès des équipes.

  • Tu documentes ce qui compte. Processus, décisions, dépendances, évolutions fonctionnelles : ce que tu laisses derrière toi tient sans toi.

  • Tu participes à la vie d'Hubvisory. Tu consolides ta posture de consultant, tu partages tes retours d'expérience et tu évolues, selon tes aspirations, vers des rôles de Product Leader ou Manager Conseil.

  • Tu as travaillé sur des briques IA (recommandation, agents, GenAI) ou tu as une appétence réelle pour intégrer l'IA au cycle produit. On cherche des PM qui qualifient les cas IA avant de les mettre en place, pas des PM qui militeraient pour de l'IA partout.

👉 Pourquoi rejoindre Hubvisory ?

  • Hubvisory est le seul cabinet en France focalisé exclusivement sur le Product Management et l'IA. Pas de practice data généraliste, pas de conseil en transformation sur tous les sujets. On fait une chose, on la fait bien.

  • Un parcours d'accompagnement sur-mesure. Nos rituels collectifs (Hub'Times) et nos revalorisations bi-annuelles récompensent la vraie progression, pas l'ancienneté.

  • Une communauté interne engagée : 20% des collaborateurs se sont volontairement engagés à travers plus de 20 projets à impact menés depuis 2022 (mécénat de compétence, organisation de maraudes, fresque du climat, etc.)

  • Des valeurs fortes : depuis 10 ans, Hubvisory grandit autour de la bienveillance, la méritocratie, l'ambition, l'expertise et l'apprentissage.

Le package : 44.000-52.000€ fixe brut, revalorisations bi-annuelles, intéressement jusqu'à 22% des profits redistribué de façon égalitaire.


Pré-requis du poste

👉 Le profil que nous recherchons

  • Tu justifies d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience en tant que Product Manager ou Product Owner sur des produits digitaux, dont une expérience significative en écosystème complexe : plusieurs métiers, plusieurs systèmes, des décisions qui ne se prennent jamais seul.

  • Tu sais mener un sujet produit de la discovery aux critères d'acceptation, et tu as déjà porté une vision et une feuille de route face à des parties prenantes exigeantes.

  • Ta maturité data est réelle : tu interprètes toi-même les chiffres, tu structures des hypothèses, tu mesures pour décider.

  • Tu es à l'aise pour contribuer au cadrage fonctionnel de briques applicatives structurantes, sans y perdre ta hauteur de vue produit.

  • Un passage par le commerce, le e-commerce ou la supply chain, en particulier sur les sujets d'offre et de référencement, est un vrai plus. Une familiarité avec un progiciel de gestion de type SAP également.

  • Trois qualités qui font la différence ici : une posture conseil assumée, une excellente communication client et une rigueur analytique à toute épreuve. Anglais professionnel.

Comment se déroule le processus de recrutement ?

  • Étape 1 : Echange avec un RH pour valider l'adéquation entre ton projet et notre modèle

  • Etape 2 : Validation de tes hard skills avec cas pratique avec un manager

  • Étape 3 : Validation de tes soft skills avec un entretien avec un VP

Quelle que soit l'issue de ton process, tu reçois un retour de notre part sous 7 jours maximum !

Si tu veux plus d’information sur notre processus de recrutement, on en a fait un article sur notre blog.

description:

  • Développer une compréhension du processus d’exploitation commerciale de résultats de recherche afin de contribuer à la coopération entre la recherche académique, la recherche industrielle et les secteurs de production.

  • Réaliser, dans son champ de compétences scientifiques et techniques, des actions destinées à accompagner des entreprises ou l’incubateur de l’école afin de favoriser la création de spin off et le développement d’entreprises technologiques.

description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant qu’Expert.e métier DataSpaceLab, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en développement, recherche et innovation rattaché à la Direction du Développement et des relations avec les Entreprises (DVE). Vous y conjuguez développement de partenariats, innovation et impact sociétal au service des grands enjeux industriels et de santé.

Le Data Space Lab est la brique opérationnelle du Hub France de Gaia-X, l’initiative européenne de référence pour les espaces de données et la souveraineté numérique, porté par l’Institut Mines-Télécom.

À Mines Saint-Étienne, il s’adosse aux centres de recherche de l’École et à leurs domaines d’excellence : ingénierie de la santé (CIS), industrie du futur et microélectronique, matériaux et procédés, énergie et environnement.

L’enjeu : faire émerger des espaces de données métiers au service de ces filières, au premier rang desquelles la santé et l’industrie du futur, en lien avec l’écosystème industriel et territorial.

 

Ce recrutement vise à doter Mines Saint-Étienne d’un.e expert.e métier capable de structurer, sur le territoire et en lien avec l’écosystème national Gaia-X, des cas d’usage et des démonstrateurs d’espaces de données, en valorisant les domaines d’excellence de l’École, au premier rang desquels la santé et l’industrie du futur.

  • Vous assurez le développement et l’animation du Data Space Lab à Saint-Étienne, en faisant comprendre Gaia-X et les espaces de données aux entreprises (PME et ETI), aux collectivités et aux acteurs du territoire.

  • Vous participez au montage de projets régionaux, nationaux et européens (Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, Bpifrance « espaces de données ») avec les équipes de l’IMT et des partenaires industriels et territoriaux.

  • Vous contribuez à la spécification des cas d’usage et à l’émergence de démonstrateurs concrets d’espaces de données métiers, dans les domaines d’excellence de Mines Saint-Étienne — santé et bien-être (CIS), industrie du futur, énergie et environnement, transport et logistique, ainsi qu’à la structuration et à l’animation d’un écosystème de partenaires (événements, communautés scientifiques de l’IMT, Caisse des Dépôts).

  • Vous rendez compte au Directeur du développement et travaillez en lien fonctionnel étroit avec les deux autres chargés de développement filière (IMT Atlantique et DG IMT) et le coordinateur national du Data Space Lab.

  • Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer recherche, monde industriel et acteurs territoriaux sera essentielle pour réussir.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Vous êtes titulaire d’un :

·           Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent

Et idéalement :

·           Titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’école de commerce (Bac+5)

·           Avec une expérience de 3 à 5 ans dans le montage de projets collaboratifs ou le développement de partenariats

•           Une expérience significative en montage de projets collaboratifs nationaux et/ou européens

•           Une expérience confirmée en tant que chargé d’affaires ou en développement commercial

•           Une expertise avérée en gestion de projet et coordination d’écosystèmes d’acteurs

•           Une maîtrise de l’anglais (niveau C1) et une grande aisance rédactionnelle

Vos atouts supplémentaires :
